Marissa, thanks for the recap. Confirming numbers from our side:

- Pilot (internal teams): ~2.5M tokens/month; MAU ~1.2k; avg tokens/call closer to 150 (includes short context + explanation snippet).
- Production target (6-12 months): 35M tokens/month; MAU ~15k.
- Budget: pilot $7k-10k/mo; if we get to production scale we expect $40k-60k/mo budgeted for inference and associated platform costs.

Two asks from us:
1) Can you model unit economics for three scenarios (pilot, ramp, production) with a target of 60%+ gross margin after inference cost?
2) Can you provide a target $/1M tokens that would make the feature ROI-positive vs our estimated revenue per feature?

I've copied our finance lead to loop her in once we have numbers (she'll want the CAC payback and LTV assumptions).

Subject: Re: Unit economics - follow-up and pricing qualification (FintechX)

Perfect, thanks for the clarity, Priya. I put together an initial unit-econ sketch and attached the template + a short notes doc. High level summary below (we'll produce a spreadsheet with line-item math):

Assumptions (pilot / ramp / production):
- Tokens/month: 2.5M / 15M / 35M
- Avg tokens per call: 150
- Revenue per feature (avg estimated incremental rev): $0.08 / call (this is your placeholder; flag if different)
- CAC and funnel: assume CAC $480 per paid account initially, avg revenue per paid account $1,800/mo at production (you'll provide finance inputs)

Preliminary costs (using conservative Redwood hosted inference estimates):
- Inference cost (approx): $420 / 1M tokens (pilot) -> scale discounts reduce this to $320 / 1M tokens at production scale (these are modeled numbers; Ben will provide firm quotes after we confirm model/config)

Key outputs we modeled:
- $/feature (inference-only cost per call): inference cost per call = (tokens per call / 1,000,000) * $/1M tokens.
  - With 150 tokens/call and $420 / 1M: cost/call = (150/1,000,000)*420 = $0.063
  - If revenue per feature = $0.08, gross margin (inference-only) = 21% at pilot pricing; not sufficient.
  - At production pricing ($320 / 1M): cost/call = (150/1,000,000)*320 = $0.048 -> margin = 40% (still below 60% target).

- To hit 60% gross margin at 150 tokens/call and $0.08 revenue per feature, we need inference cost <= $0.032 per call -> equivalent to ~ $213 / 1M tokens.

- CAC payback (months) example: if net contribution per account = (ARPA - inference run rate attributable) and ARPA = $1,800/mo (production), with inference share ~10% of ARPA at production -> net contribution ~$1,620 -> CAC $480 -> payback ~0.3 months (very healthy). For small pilots ARPA will be lower and payback longer; we'll illustrate with a 6/12/24-month CAC horizon.

Next steps I propose:
1) Ben and Dev to review the inference configuration (batching, quantization, caching) and give firm $/1M quotes for pilot and production.
2) I'll share the filled template + a short SOW draft for pilot scope and success criteria.
3) Priya please share finance contact and any LTV assumptions you want us to use.

Ben / Dev pinging you for the price/optimizations side.

Thanks
Marissa

Priya / Marissa

Quick technical/pricing note from the infra side: we can likely get to the $320 / 1M tokens figure at ~15-35M tokens/mo with config:
- FP16 quantization + optimized kernel dispatching
- Host-level KV caching for common prefixes (saves ~30% on repeated flows)
- Autoscale policy tuned for consistent p95 latency (target 250-300ms)

If FintechX is willing to commit to a 6-12 month reserved capacity with a modest commit, we can move pricing toward ~$230 / 1M tokens which is in the neighborhood of the $213 / 1M you'd need for 60% margin at $0.08 revenue/feature.

I'll follow up with a short quote sheet and a couple of config options (pilot vs committed).

Ben
